concepts.name: Sales funnel stages
concepts.summary: Recall the main stages a prospect moves through from awareness to closed deal and what happens at each.

concepts.name: Prospects versus leads
concepts.summary: Explain the difference between a raw contact, a lead, a qualified prospect and a customer.

concepts.name: Value proposition
concepts.summary: Explain in a sentence what problem the product solves for a buyer and the benefit they gain.

concepts.name: Features versus benefits
concepts.summary: Distinguish what a product does from what that does for the buyer and translate one into the other.

concepts.name: Sales roles and quota
concepts.summary: Describe common sales roles and what a quota measures.

concepts.name: Ideal customer profile
concepts.summary: Explain how an ideal customer profile defines which companies and people are worth pursuing.

concepts.name: Outreach channels
concepts.summary: Name the common outreach channels such as phone, email, social and referrals and when each is typically used.

misconceptions.text: Selling is mainly about persuading people to buy something they do not need.
Anyone who could possibly use the product is a good lead.
Listing every product feature is the best way to show value.

concepts.name: Lead sourcing and research
concepts.summary: Build a list of leads matching the ICP and research each for a relevant trigger or context.

concepts.name: Writing cold outreach messages
concepts.summary: Write a short, personalised cold email or message with a relevant hook and a single clear ask.

concepts.name: Cold call opening
concepts.summary: Open a cold call with a brief introduction, a reason for calling and a request for permission to continue.

concepts.name: Open and probing questions
concepts.summary: Use open and follow-up questions to draw out a buyer's situation rather than closed yes/no questions.

concepts.name: Basic lead qualification
concepts.summary: Use criteria such as budget, authority, need and timing to decide whether a lead is worth pursuing.

concepts.name: CRM record keeping
concepts.summary: Log contacts, activities, notes and deal stages in a CRM so the record is accurate and usable by others.

concepts.name: Scripted objection responses
concepts.summary: Respond to common objections such as price or timing using acknowledge, question and respond patterns.

misconceptions.text: A cold email works best when it is long and explains everything about the product.
Most objections mean the buyer is saying no for good.
CRM updates are admin that can wait until the deal closes.

concepts.name: Discovery call structure
concepts.summary: Plan and run a discovery call that covers current situation, pain, impact, decision process and next steps.

concepts.name: Pain and impact quantification
concepts.summary: Analyse a buyer's problem to estimate its business cost and tie it to the value of solving it.

concepts.name: Tailored pitch and demo
concepts.summary: Shape a pitch or demo around the pains uncovered in discovery rather than a generic feature tour.

concepts.name: Stakeholder and buying committee mapping
concepts.summary: Identify the champion, economic buyer, users and blockers and how each influences the decision.

concepts.name: Diagnosing objections
concepts.summary: Separate stated objections from underlying concerns and choose a response that addresses the real cause.

concepts.name: Closing techniques and next steps
concepts.summary: Ask for commitment at the right moment and secure a dated, specific next step after every interaction.

concepts.name: Pipeline stage criteria
concepts.summary: Judge whether a deal truly meets the criteria for its stage and keep close dates and amounts realistic.

concepts.name: Follow-up cadence
concepts.summary: Plan follow-up touches across channels that add new value rather than just checking in.

misconceptions.text: A discovery call is a chance to talk through the product and pitch early.
Talking to one enthusiastic contact is enough to win the deal.
Moving a deal to a later stage shows progress even if the buyer has not met the stage criteria.

concepts.name: Deal qualification frameworks
concepts.summary: Evaluate a complex deal against frameworks such as MEDDICC and decide whether to invest, adjust or disqualify.

concepts.name: Negotiation and concessions
concepts.summary: Judge when and how to trade concessions for commitments while protecting value and margin.

concepts.name: Competitive positioning
concepts.summary: Assess a competitor's strengths and weaknesses and position against them without disparaging.

concepts.name: Territory and account planning
concepts.summary: Analyse accounts and territory to prioritise effort and plan multi-stage campaigns toward target accounts.

concepts.name: Win-loss analysis
concepts.summary: Examine won and lost deals to find patterns in qualification, process and positioning.

concepts.name: Funnel metrics diagnosis
concepts.summary: Diagnose where the funnel leaks using conversion rates, cycle length and average deal size and choose a fix.

concepts.name: Sales forecasting
concepts.summary: Analyse pipeline coverage, stage conversion rates and deal age to produce a defensible forecast against quota.

misconceptions.text: A large pipeline guarantees hitting quota regardless of deal quality.
Discounting is the quickest way to close and costs little.
Criticising competitors is the strongest way to differentiate.

concepts.name: Designing a sales process
concepts.summary: Create a repeatable sales process with stages, exit criteria and playbooks fitted to a market and deal type.

concepts.name: Go-to-market and segmentation strategy
concepts.summary: Design which segments, channels and motions such as inbound, outbound or partner a company should pursue.

concepts.name: Quota and compensation design
concepts.summary: Evaluate how quotas and incentives shape seller behaviour and set them to be achievable and aligned with strategy.

concepts.name: Coaching and enablement systems
concepts.summary: Build coaching, call review and training programs that raise team performance measurably.

concepts.name: Strategic enterprise deal leadership
concepts.summary: Judge and steer large multi-party deals including executive sponsorship, procurement and risk.

concepts.name: Revenue operations and tooling
concepts.summary: Design CRM data models, handoffs and reporting that align sales, marketing and customer success.

concepts.name: Pricing and packaging strategy
concepts.summary: Evaluate pricing and packaging models against buyer value, competition and sales motion.

misconceptions.text: Top individual sellers make the best managers and coaches without further training.
Higher quotas and bigger commissions always drive better performance.
A single sales process works for every segment and deal size.
